Welcome

A note from Marina & Lucas

Dear Guest,

Welcome to Bearadise, and thank you for choosing our cabin! We're a mother-son duo, Marina and Lucas, who live in Miami and Chicago respectively. As we're sure many of you can relate to, we have a very typical mother-son relationship, but we decided to buy this cabin together anyway, as somewhere to spend time with friends and family and to hike in the mountains.

After a long day in the mountains or nearby towns, we hope you can relax on the deck, in the hot tub, or just sit back and enjoy the bar and game room. There are plenty of board games and cards for those waiting their turn to run the pool table!

Our goal was to create a beautiful, inviting environment where everyone can enjoy all this wonderful area has to offer. We hope the time we dedicated to creating a fun and enjoyable space is reflected in your stay. If you have any suggestions or advice, we'd genuinely love to hear how we could make Bearadise even better.

In conclusion, we hope you have a fun, relaxing, and above all safe stay. Please always feel free to reach out to us through the app.

✦ Meet Your Hosts
Lucas
Vegan. Once ate two Chipotle bowls in one sitting. Converted a school bus into a camper.
Marina
Lucas is her oldest; she also has twin boys. Loves reading, traveling, walking, and Greek dancing.
✦ Getting Here

The cabin sits up in the mountains, so expect some steep inclines, winding curves, and one blind curve and one blind slope along the way. While it can feel intimidating at first, the streets are safe and you do not need an SUV or 4-wheel drive to get here. Everyone respects the speed limit and the roads are salted in the winter. If you're driving at night, keep in mind that most roads aren't well lit, so please drive slowly and carefully.

When you reach the cabin, you'll see a driveway right in front of the front porch. You can park either perpendicularly (head first), which fits 5 to 6 cars, or parallel to the cabin, which fits about 3. You can also park on the gravel by the picnic table.

📓
Please tell us about your stay! There's a blue Experience Notebook in the cabin where you can share feedback, favorite restaurants, and what you got up to. It helps future guests, and we love reading them too.

Check-in and check-out times are strictly enforced so we have enough time between guests. There are times when guests are checking in the same day others check out, and that window is crucial to cleaning and resetting everything. After the 10-minute grace period, late checkouts are subject to a $100 fine, plus an additional $100 for each hour after.

✦ Address

1512 Ginnys Trail, Sevierville, TN 37876

✦ Parking

There's a driveway right in front of the front porch. Park either perpendicularly (head first), which fits 5 to 6 cars, or parallel to the cabin, which fits about 3. You can also park on the gravel by the picnic table.

✦ Checking In

The cabin has an electronic lock. Your access code was sent in your welcome message. Enter the code, wait for the checkmark to flash along with the confirmation chime, and then open the door.

✦ Checking Out
  1. Leave the laundry to us: bed as-is, towels on the first floor bathroom floor.
  2. Please start the dishwasher before leaving.
  3. Remove all items from the refrigerator and place all trash bags in the bear-safe trash cans outside, by the sign. Please knot the trash bags first; this limits odor and helps keep bears away (see the Bear Safety section). The lock code is 7222.
  4. If you used the grill, please don't leave any charcoal behind.
  5. Make sure all lights are off, windows are closed, doors are locked, and everything is back in its place.
  6. Drive safely!
🔒
Always lock the cabin and car doors. Bears have a sense of smell far better than a dog's and have opened unlocked car doors or climbed through open sunroofs to get to food inside; this has happened here before.
🤝

Safety & Evacuation

Please read before your first night
🚨
In any emergency, call 911 immediately. The cabin address is 1512 Ginnys Trail, Sevierville, TN 37876.
✦ Fire Extinguishers

There is a fire extinguisher on each level:

  • Basement: in the HVAC closet, right across from the door to the deck
  • Main Floor: underneath the kitchen sink
  • Loft: in the laundry room
✦ Detectors & First Aid

There are smoke detectors in each bedroom and in the living areas, plus a carbon monoxide detector in the kitchen. The first aid kit is located under the kitchen sink and includes adhesive fabric and plastic bandages, antibiotic ointments, BZK antiseptic towelettes, burn cream packets, aspirin, ibuprofen, gauze roll and pads, wound closures, a cold pack, and other multi-use first aid items.

Bear Safety

You're in black bear country: here's how to stay safe
🐾
Bears have been seen at this cabin before. Please take these steps seriously: never leave food in your car, always lock car doors, and never leave food or trash out on the deck.

The Smoky Mountains are home to American black bears, one of the largest predators in the park, though the vast majority of their diet is actually berries, nuts, and plants. According to the National Park Service, black bears are highly intelligent and can identify food by both smell and sight, not just scent.

✦ Why This Matters

Bears that get into human food or trash quickly lose their natural fear of people and start associating cars, coolers, and cabins with an easy meal. These "food conditioned" bears become more dangerous to guests and, sadly, are often the ones that end up euthanized. Keeping food secured protects both you and the bears.

✦ At the Cabin
  • Lock your car doors at all times: bears can open unlocked doors or climb through a cracked window or open sunroof, and have done so here before.
  • Never leave food, coolers, or scented items in your car: this includes drinks, snacks, sunscreen, and toiletries, not just meals.
  • Keep all food inside the cabin with doors and windows closed when you're not in the room, since bears can push through an open door or window.
  • Nothing food related on the deck: no coolers, food left out, or trash bags, even briefly.
  • Knot all trash bags before placing them in the bear-safe cans: loose bags attract bears through smell far more than sealed ones.
  • Wash dirty dishes promptly rather than leaving them out overnight.
👀
If you do spot a bear from a distance, enjoy the moment from inside; do not approach, feed, or try to photograph it up close. Learn more from the NPS black bear safety page.
♨️

Hot Tub & Jacuzzi

Two ways to soak during your stay
🔞
The hot tub and jacuzzi are for guests 25 and over, or those accompanied by a parent, and are used at your own risk. No alcohol or drugs at or near the hot tub; heat speeds up their effects and can cause unconsciousness.
✦ Hot Tub
  • If you've been drinking, we recommend skipping the hot tub; leave immediately if you feel uncomfortable or sleepy.
  • Please don't lean against the trellis (the privacy wall by the hot tub).
  • You sweat out fluids in the water without noticing, so stay extra hydrated.
✦ Master Bedroom Jacuzzi

The primary bedroom has its own private jacuzzi for a quieter soak, on the same guests-25-and-over basis as the hot tub above.

🔌

Technology

Wifi, TVs, fireplace, thermostat, lights
✦ Wifi
Network
Bearadise
Password
EnjoyYourStay!

The modem and main router are located by the TV. There are additional routers in the basement and loft to keep the connection strong on every floor.

✦ TVs

Each bedroom has a Vizio TV with Smartcast. The living room has a 50" Roku TV with Guest Mode enabled: simply enter your checkout date when you turn it on, and the rest is taken care of for you.

✦ Thermostat

Located on the living room wall, right by the kitchen. Please try to keep it between 68 and 78 degrees, and don't leave the A/C running when you leave the cabin.

✦ Fireplace

The gas log fireplace should already be on; just turn the timer on the top right of the fireplace to set how long you'd like it running.

✦ Lights

The light strip under the bar is controlled by the remote on the bar or the one underneath the TV. All deck lights are on a dusk-to-dawn timer; they're LED and weatherproof, so no need to worry about weather damage or overheating.

✦ Locking Up

Unlock: enter your code, wait for the checkmark and chime, open the door.
Lock: close the door and press the lock button on the bottom right.
